titolo: How One Trader Destroyed Barings Bank

shots.voce: One trader lost eight hundred and twenty-seven million pounds, and destroyed a bank two hundred and thirty-three years old.
How did one man hide it from everyone?
Barings was founded in seventeen sixty-two.
It financed governments, and even banked for the Queen.
Nick Leeson joined Barings in nineteen eighty-eight.
In Singapore he ran both trading and settlement, the desks that should check each other.
Losses went into a hidden account, number eight eight eight eight eight.
He bet on the Nikkei, Japan's stock index.
Then, on January seventeenth, nineteen ninety-five, the Kobe earthquake struck.
shots.sotto: Japanese markets fell sharply that week

shots.voce: He doubled down, and the market kept falling.
The losses grew larger than the bank's entire capital.
On February twenty-third, Leeson left Singapore.
shots.sotto: He left a note reading: I'm sorry

shots.voce: Days later, on February twenty-sixth, the Bank of England could find no rescue.
Dutch bank ING bought it for one pound.
So the answer was simple: nobody checked.
Leeson was jailed for six and a half years.

_correzioni: Opening: Barings was 233 years old in 1995 (1762 to 1995) - correct, kept.
Barings capital: reported capital was about £440M (Bank of England report cites ~£440M); kept.
Singapore posting: Leeson was posted to Singapore in 1992 - correct, kept.
Age in 1995: Leeson was born February 1967, so he was 27 for most of 1995 and turned 28 on 25 Feb 1995 - changed to 27 to be safe at the time of the collapse.
Account 88888: account was opened in 1992 - correct, kept.
Queen/Royal Family: Barings banked for the Queen - correct, kept.
Kobe earthquake: struck 17 January 1995 - correct, kept.
Leeson left Singapore on 23 February 1995 - correct, kept.
Bank of England rescue: the Bank failed to find a rescue on Sunday 26 Feb 1995 - correct, kept.
ING paid £1 on 6 March 1995 (assuming Barings' liabilities) - 'Days later' was fine for administration, but the ING purchase was a week later; no change needed to the voice line.
Leeson's sentence: six and a half years, sentenced December 1995 - correct, kept.
Leeson's note: the note read 'I'm sorry' - correct, kept.

The £827M loss figure is widely cited (about £827M, $1.4B) - kept; source labels changed to Bank of England Report where claims are only partly from that report: ING £1 price source changed to 'Court filings and press reports, 1995'.
Dossier ROLE: Leeson was a futures/derivatives trader and also head of settlement - kept.
